utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to correct the transcript. I said information of threats per se are not uncommon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness please be brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning, and please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please. Examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, can you tell the Chamber your full name and your date of birth, please?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was born on 29 December, 1957, in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber of your education, how far you got with your schooling?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: After completing primary school, I completed the secondary school of electrical engineering and then the electrical engineering college in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you complete your studies?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I completed my studies in 1986.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever work in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I worked at the wicker furniture factory that was called TPN Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you start working there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I started working there on the 27th of January, 1987.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work there right up until the events of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I worked there until April 17th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What position did you achieve at the wicker factory?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I achieved the position of the general director of this company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About a year before April, 1992, did the company have any sort of financial difficulties?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it enter into bankruptcy?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Its accounts were blocked and after the strikes, the workers appointed me for the general manager, and then after the decision of the upper court in Bijeljina, I was appointed the receiver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any role to play in the commercial consequences of the bankruptcy?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When I was appointed the receiver, the bankruptcy council appointed an external expert in economy and Milan Simic, as a successful economist, was doing this work for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you perform military service in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that and where was that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I performed military service in 1984 in Kiseljak, by Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you specialize in any particular aspect of the military arts?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. I was a regular soldier in an artillery unit. I did not have a rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still have family living in the Bosanski Samac area?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My family lives in a village ten kilometres from Bosanski Samac, the village is called Donja Slatina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who lives there? Which family members?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: My old and sick grandmother. My mother who is also sick and two sisters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do the sisters work?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: One sister works for a company called Mebos that manufactures water heaters. And the other sister works at the Republic Customs Administration in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about some of the personalities in this case. Do you know Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long would you say that you've known him?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I've known him since four or five years from before the war, but we were never close friends at that time. I just knew him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: May I ask a question? Mr. Prosecutor, Di Fazio, I would like to ask a question about the other members of the witness -- if my memory serves me right, he has a wife and children, and I would like to ask he doesn't have to define the place where they are living more in detail, but are they living outside the former Yugoslavia. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honour pleases, I will ask the question of course, but my understanding, the witness will tell us anyway, but my understanding is he's not married but I'll ask him and we'll see what the situation is if Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard his honour's question, what's your marital situation? Are you currently married? Have you ever been married and do you have kids -- children, rather?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I have never been officially married. I have no children but there is a lady that I lived with, we are not married, but we are in touch, we have been in touch for sometime, and she lives in Belgrade. She does not live in the territory of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. While we are on this topic, does she -- everyone understand that is you're currently serving your prison sentence, does she maintain contact with you while you're still in custody?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she does. She is waiting for a Spanish visa to come and visit me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we were -- I was asking you about the -- some of the personalities and I was asking you about Mr. Blagoje Simic. You said you've known him for five years. In what -- under what circumstances did you meet him and under what circumstances did you associate with him in those five years before April, 1992? Was it professional dealings? Were you his patient, or political meetings, or simply in the cafes or how?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, just before the multi-party elections, I knew him but not much, and we would just meet in different discos and in cafes. On the 2nd of August, I don't know if it was of 1990 or 1991, that was the time when I was closer friends with him, but this lasted for a very short time period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a look around the room and see if you can identify him. If you can, please let us know.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise him. He's sitting in the middle. He has a goatee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the record indicate that Mr. Todorovic has successfully identified Mr. Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just small correction, Your Honours in transcript maybe I misunderstood it, in transcript it says he has a goatee. In fact the witness said my client has academic beard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Academic beard?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. This will be different from goatee beard, so could my friend clarify it? MR. DI FAZIO: I think an academic beard is a goatee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will depend on the interpreter's -- please go ahead, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Miroslav Tadic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him, would you say?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I met Miroslav Tadic when I was in secondary school. He was a teacher at that secondary school and that's where I met him. Afterwards, I would see him around but we were never close friends, but I knew him, I just knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say after you would see him around, do you mean he was just an acquaintance whom you might nod to in the street but you didn't socialise? Can you give us any more idea of your relationship with him?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we didn't socialise. We would greet each other on the street if we met, but we met infrequently because I was in college and my interests were different, but sometimes when I would meet him we would greet, but there was nothing special about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. His nickname was "Brko."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again can you go through the same exercise, look around the room, see if you can identify him, and if you can, please let us know.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see him. He has a mustache, a grey -- grey hair and he's wearing glasses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the record indicate that the witness identified Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Simo Zaric, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I have known him for about ten years. I had heard of him before and I knew him by sight but I didn't socialise with him up until a year or two before the war. One of his friends was the commercial manager in my factory and we would greet each other a couple of times, so I knew of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the friend you're talking about? What's the name of the person?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Anto Ivanovic, nicknamed "Tosa."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Can you look around the room and see if you can identify him, please?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just give us a brief description so that we can be sure that you've correctly identified him.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He is grey haired, he has glasses, he has a light blue shirt and a dark blue jacket on. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Could the record indicate that Mr. Todorovic has identified Mr. Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From everything that you ever told us so far, it appears that you had no experience up until April of 1992 in any form of police matters or security matters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ever trained as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ever applied for a job as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever had any particular interest, even as a hobby, in police matters?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever tell people that you were particularly skilled or qualified in police matters, acting as a policeman, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I think I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the political backgrounds of the men that I've asked you about so far. Mr. Blagoje Simic, was he a member of any particular political party?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was a member of the Serbian Democratic Party. From 1990 or 1991, since -- from the moment it was founded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been aware of his being a member of any other political party before that, or is that all you know?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was only in that party. I have no knowledge that he was in any other party. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, there is an error in the transcript and I want it corrected if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Line ten on page 14, I heard the witness say from the moment it was founded -- founded. In other words from its inception. I'll ask the witness again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think, yes, clarify that with the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: I just want to make sure that the transcript is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, I understood you to say that Mr. Blagoje Simic was a member of the Serbian democratic party from 1990 or 1991, since the time it was founded. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I said. Maybe -- but to be precise, maybe not from the first day it was founded. Maybe from the first, second or third month of its inception.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, early on in its beginnings.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea of the political background of Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, that is, I did not know that Miroslav Tadic was politically engaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you didn't know that he was politically engaged, what precisely do you mean? That he wasn't an active politician of any sort or something else?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I did not know that he was a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about Simo Zaric? Have you any idea of what his political background was?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I knew, he was a member of the League of Communists at the time when that party existed. But prior to the multi-party elections, that party was -- had the abbreviation of SDP. It was SDP of Bosnia and Herzegovina but it was really the continuation of that previous party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the previous party, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When saying "the previous party" I mean the League of Communists for Yugoslavia which for 50 years was the only party in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about your political background. First of all, can you tell us if you were ever a member of the League of Communists?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. I was never a member of the League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your view about the Communist Party and your view about communism generally?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I had a negative attitude, because with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio is that relevant? MR. DI FAZIO: Only because of subsequent testimony that the witness will give. I don't intend to dwell on it by any means, I can deal with it in one answer, that's all. I'm not going to investigate the political background of all these people for any other purpose --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't want us to go into the verse and chapter of communism. MR. DI FAZIO: I certainly don't want to do that either, if Your Honours please, I'll be as brief as I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just heard the exchange between myself and the Chamber. I want to be brief about this. Were you an anti-communist? Can you answer -- you have to it have an oral answer so it can be recorded.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that fact known?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Let me add, I was a passive anti-communist. I didn't sympathise with that party, and I was an anti-communist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm more interested in was that fact, your view about that, known at least amongst your circle of friends and people who knew you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It certainly was known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1990 or 1991, what position did he hold?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: You mean in the political sense?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: If I recollect well, he was one of the municipal vice-presidents of the Serbian Democratic -- SDS, Serb Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you ever join the Serb Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That was on the 2nd of August. My -- 1990 or 1991, I cannot recollect, 1990 or 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you come to join the SDS?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When my friends left from my celebration, I went to the cultural hall in the village and when I enter that conference hall, they proposed me as the President of that local council of SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from your answer, this particular day, the 2nd of August, you were having some sort of private function and then you went down to this conference hall where the SDS conference was taking place?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who selected you or nominated you for a position in the SDS?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Some of the inhabitants of that village. They said that I was educated, an anti-communist and they immediately asked me to be the President of that local board. I didn't want -- I didn't dare turn them down, and then I accepted this position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to now turn from this issue to ask you to provide the Chamber with a broad outline of the last ten years or so, we will be returning to a lot of these topics later, but it's generally agreed in this case that you were appointed police chief. Can you recall just the date that that occurred?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I was appointed on the 28th or 29th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever gain membership of subsequently of a body called a "Crisis Staff"?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was between the 15th and the 17th of April. Somewhere between these two days, the 15th or the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I have a question here. When you asked when the witness was appointed police chief, I would ask who did he replace and for what reason? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Very well. I'll clarify that issue, if Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, in March of 1992, were Serbs in Bosanski Samac in the process of setting up parallel organs of state, parallel to the already-existing organs?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, [Interpretation] I believe that this witness is not a lawyer and that this language of the Prosecutor cannot be used as such and that the question has to be rephrased, and the witness doesn't know what the relationship between the various bodies and what they are, and it would require some assumptions of this witness, and this is the basis of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The objection is overruled. The Trial Chamber doesn't see anything wrong with this question because these are matters within the knowledge of the witness. The Prosecution will continue. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: About that time that you were appointed police chief, were Serbs in Bosanski Samac in the process of setting up parallel organs of state, for example, police forces and so on?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At the assembly of the Serb people on the 28th of February, the municipality -- Serb Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo was in the process of being founded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were appointed as police chief, was that as, to put it broadly speaking and it's only broadly speaking, a Serbian police chief?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I believe yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time that you were appointed to this position, was there already a police chief operating and carrying out his job and his functions? I think --

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that part of the municipality that had existed for some -- for years in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: There were two. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, parallel organisations, parallel developments, if Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll be returning to this topic later, if Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we were talking about your membership of the Crisis Staff. Did that continue essentially throughout 1992?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point, in 1992, did the Crisis Staff change its name?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It changed its name but that was later. I don't know the exact date of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it change its name to something called a "War Presidency"?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at this document that I produce to you? MR. DI FAZIO: I've got copies of the original and translations for the Court. And if Your Honours please, Defence counsel will know of this document as C69 in the list of exhibits. Do Your Honours have copies now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, I know you don't read too well because of your eye sight, and this document is hard to read, so you get down and have a -- closely and look at it if need be, okay? Can you see it? I don't expect you read all of this, but I'll take you through it and it's in paragraph 1, it's paragraph 168 that I'm interested in, not 169, which is also on the same page. So let's look at 168. It's entitled "Decision on the formation of War Presidencies in municipalities in times of war. " Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it then goes on to set out the circumstances in which War Presidencies shall be formed and I think you can see that in Article 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But for the defendant, I would like to have the B/C/S version placed on the ELMO, for the benefit of the defendants. MR. DI FAZIO: I may have an extra copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, an extra copy can be put on the ELMO. MR. DI FAZIO: We did provide five to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I received four B/C/S versions, three for the Chamber, I gave one to the LO, the registry doesn't have one, and -- MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps mine can be used. I won't be dwelling long on this document, I might add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Really, Mr. Todorovic, the article I'm interested in is Article 5. Have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That says, "War Presidencies shall be formed within 15 days of the decision, of this decision, and on that day, Crisis Staffs cease to operate." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that basically what happened in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that people who were essentially, or rather, the Crisis Staff continued with the same people but just changed its name, instead of being a Crisis Staff it became a War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Only the name was changed but the people remained the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's signed by apparently by Dr. Radovan Karadzic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do see the name Radovan Karadzic, but I do not see the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's dated the 31st of May, 1992. How does that accord with your memory? Did the Crisis Staff change its name to a War Presidency around June? Would that be right? Or do you think it was later?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly the date when this -- the change occurred, but I know that later, it was called a War Presidency, but I cannot recall the exact date. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I produce the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any objection from the Defence? I see that there is none. Can we have the number, please, from the registry?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The English version is P72. And the B/C/S will be P72 ter. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I've finished with the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, just a small correction maybe, as I said, maybe I'm wrong but in Article 2 of this decision, in B/C/S language, it says, the Article 2 reads as follows: [Interpretation] the War Presidency shall consist of the trustee of the republic and as a rule, and this as a rule, was translated in the English text as "generally, and generally" and I'm objecting this as a matter of principle because I believe that "generally" does not correspond to the spirit of this article, which here contains this instead of "generally" "as a rule." "As a rule" might be more appropriate in that sense in Article 2 of that particular decision, which is something different than "generally." MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours want a response from me on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If any. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't think I can respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the Trial Chamber can simply ask for -- MR. DI FAZIO: It's a question of translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, from the translation unit. MR. DI FAZIO: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will simply ask from the translation unit. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On the basis of what Mr. Pantelic has said. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But the Trial Chamber will accept the translation from the translation unit of the Tribunal. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just while I'm on this topic of the change of name I'd like to produce another document to the witness which I now do, Defence counsel will know this document as C78.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, we have C78 part 2. Maybe our friends from Prosecution can indicate whether we are going to speak about part 1 C78 or part 2? Because I don't see in my -- MR. DI FAZIO: No, there is only one document, C78, and one document only, C78, part 2 is something to do with the way my case manager organised the file but we are only dealing with C78.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to look at that document, Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm still looking at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can I just ask you, that --

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This appears to be what it says, decision on renaming the municipal Crisis Staff, suggesting that it's going to be renamed the War Presidency on the date of this decision, which is the 21st of July, 1992. Do you recall that change in name from Crisis Staff to War Presidency being adopted in this way?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's apparently signed by Dr. Blagoje Simic. However, would you look at the signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not a handwriting specialist but I don't believe that this is the signature of Blagoje Simic, concretely this example here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I have no quarrel with that. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in principle, we don't have objections. These are the decisions, everything is clear, but just for the sake of justice, we kindly ask for the time being that these documents would be with ID numbers so that we can check the English translation and the spirit of this translation in accordance with the law, with the law language. I have a great sympathy and I appreciate the translation unit people, but still, because we are speaking about the legal documents, we would like to check again some -- because otherwise, one point or comment or one word can have different meanings in terms of legal language. So within the testimony of this witness, we shall give our answer and it can be admitted. So as I said, I'm not objecting about the documents to be tendered there is no problem with that but still some correction may be -- could be made. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I make the application for it to be fully produced into evidence as a full exhibit. Defence have had this documentation for years now, I think. Furthermore, the matter that Mr. Pantelic raised is not a matter for refusing to admit the document into evidence. It's a matter of linguistics and translation and that can be sorted out at a later stage, if need be. Indeed, he can raise it with the witness if he has any quibble or quarrel with the way things are translated. So on that basis I seek the full admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the document will be admitted into evidence and the Trial Chamber accepts the translation from the translation unit of the Tribunal. Can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P73 and P73 ter, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we proceed? MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remain on the War Presidency throughout 1993, 1994, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I think until late 1994 or early 1995. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we take our break? MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry, I didn't realise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will take our break now and resume our proceedings at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecution can continue. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, yesterday apparently an issue was raised regarding the fifth amended indictment. Its translation. My case manager tells me it's been translated and been served so that matter has been rectified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. I see Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to raise a short issue and I would like for just for a closed session -- private session because of the question that I'm going to be asking. All I need is a private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was asking you about your appointment to various positions in Bosanski Samac throughout the mid-1990s. Did you ever receive an appointment to the executive board?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When I was appointed as chief, I was automatically, because of my position, also -- I also became a member of the executive board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about in later years, around 1995 or 1996? Did you ever receive an appointment then?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In 1995, I was appointed the vice-president of the executive board. That was my position then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. Now, when you were appointed to that position, did you receive the support, political support, of anyone?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I received the support of the municipal board members that were members of the assembly of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that include Mr. Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in order to clarify we would like to see about which time period we are speaking now. If it's 1995, it's irrelevant for this case. If something, the other -- I'm speaking about the executive board, membership in executive board. If the other time period is in question, then I kindly ask my friend to clarify that, because otherwise, I don't see the sense of membership in 1995. It's beyond the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution I'm sure is aware of that and they will clarify the period. MR. DI FAZIO: The indictment isn't it a straitjacket. I understand what the Chamber has said to us regarding leading evidence beyond the parameters of the indictment. I understand that perfectly well but the nature of the relationship between Mr. Todorovic and these defendants is of -- is crucial, and there may be matters that occur beyond -- outside of the period of the indictment, before the period of the indictment and subsequently, that shed light, shed light, on the nature of the relationship between them. That's all that I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that is accepted by the Trial Chamber because, of course, we are all aware that the building up of tensions started prior to 1992 and what you have submitted may well be true. So only to that extent. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, also if Your Honours please, continued support of this witness by defendants is also a matter that may -- that is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In these proceedings. MR. DI FAZIO: In these proceedings for the Chamber to assess events that occur earlier, prior to that continued support. So that's the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then, Mr. Di Fazio, you can continue. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June of 1997, did you go anywhere, leave Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- where did you go?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I went to Serbia, because I had some private business with a private company in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, were you aware of an indictment having been issued against you by this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: End of -- at the end of 1995, this was broadcast on the television of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the indictment was publicly broadcast, and that's when I found out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a matter of common knowledge in Bosanski Samac and all your colleagues knew of the fact that you'd been indicted?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Most people knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did that fact have anything to do with your going to Serbia, apart from -- apart from your business commitments? Were you concerned about avoiding arrest, in other words?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Among other things, that fact also contributed to me going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September of 1998, were you in effect, kidnapped or apprehended by people?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the night of 26 of September, 1998, I was kidnapped by a criminal group from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you eventually arrested in Bosnia by SFOR?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This group transferred me in a passenger vehicle. They illegally took me over Bosnia [as interpreted] in a boat, and about ten minutes later, and the phone, or through a radio transmitter, they called NATO troops and a helicopter came and this helicopter then took me to the NATO base in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you subsequently brought to The Hague and were you arraigned here on the 30th of September?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following that, was there some protracted legal argument between your Defence counsel and the Prosecution regarding all sorts of matters, including the circumstances under which you'd been arrested?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a discussion going on about the legality of my kidnapping or arrest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to go into the details of that. I'm not interested in that I just want to know whether that occurred. Did that occur?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In subsequently, did you enter a plea of guilty to a charge of persecutions?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that pursuant to a plea agreement or following upon you entering into a plea agreement with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of that agreement, did you agree to cooperate with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April and May of last year, did your lawyers make submissions on penalty to a Chamber of this Tribunal, following your plea of guilty?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 31st of July, last year, were you sentenced to ten years' imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you now currently serving that sentence in a European country?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I want to refer to the sentencing judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I believe you have copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we do. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. And I have a B/C/S copy that I'd like to produce to the witness. I don't -- just on the question of producing this into evidence, do you want me to produce it into evidence? It's a matter of course of public record, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber takes judicial notice. MR. DI FAZIO: So I don't need to produce it into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Todorovic, I think you are familiar with this document, are you not?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've read it and I think recently reread it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you go to paragraph 3, please? In the section dealing with introduction and procedural history and read it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Page 2?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll find the whole judgement has got paragraphs and I'll be referring from now on to paragraphs, and you'll find that at least in the -- after the index, the very first page of the judgement starts off with paragraph 1, 2, 3 and so on. And I'm referring to paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For the benefit of our clients it could be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Di Fazio, I was wondering what you intend to do. Is it necessary to read the paragraphs? Because they are already contained here. Is it not just sufficient to refer to them? And raise questions on them, if that's what you want to do with the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: I think that's the way I'll deal with it. I don't want him to read it into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's what I'm wondering about. MR. DI FAZIO: And then I'll take what I need out of each paragraph. Mr. Usher, do you have the B/C/S? May I approach the witness could I can indicate the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The paragraph, yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you have it now, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just have a quick read of it, reacquaint yourself with it. You -- that gives a summary of the charges that you were faced -- you were faced with when you first came, does it not?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you skip to paragraph 5, please? That indicates that on the 13th of December, 2000, you entered a plea of guilty to count 1 on the indictment against you, and the Prosecution indicated it would withdraw other counts? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, look at paragraph 9 of the judgement. Paragraph 9 sets out the factual basis of your guilty plea, does it not?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it lists all sorts of things that you engaged in, including the beating and murder of a man called Anto Brandic, various beatings, various sexual offences and so on. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And furthermore, that you participated in the unlawful detention, cruel inhumane treatment of Bosnian Croats and Muslims and other details?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Also in paragraph 10, it refers to your agreement to provide full cooperation with the Prosecution. You agree with that factual assertion there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally -- not finally, further, paragraph 11, highlights that as part of the -- withdraw that. Further, paragraph 11 highlights that there are -- a recommendation was made regarding sentence and a range of sentence. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The judgement again returns to the factual basis in paragraph 12, and it indicates more agreed facts by which the crime of persecution was perpetrated, including forcible takeover by Serb forces of various towns, murder, sexual assaults, repeated beatings, unlawful detention, confinement of non-Serbs, cruel, inhumane treatment of non-Serbs, including beatings, torture, forced labour, coercion into false -- signing false statements, deportation, issuance of orders and directives violating the rights of non-Serb civilians and so on. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you now to go towards the end of the judgement, please? Perhaps I should say about midway through? In fact the paragraph I want you to look at is paragraphs 34 to 37. The judgement again refers to forcible takeover of the municipality of Bosanski Samac. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The judgement again goes into more detail regarding murder, sexual assaults, repeated beatings. Have you seen those paragraphs and do you agree with those?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would ask you to continue looking through paragraphs 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47. Again, paragraph 41 details various beatings that you engaged in? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 41 also -- sorry, 42 also refers to unlawful detention, arrest and so on, of Croats and Muslims. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 43 refers to cruel, inhumane treatment, non-Serb civilians, beatings, torture, forced labour, confinement, do you agree with all of that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I don't need to -- you've seen paragraph 44 as well? You agree with the matters set out there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 46 -- sorry, 47 refers to plunder and looting. Do you agree with all the allegations there, the factual matters there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I agree but I did not personally participate in the lootings. It was the policemen. I just did not stop them from doing it, but other than that, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I'm done with the judgement. Now, I want to turn to an issue that I've briefly touched upon and that is your appointment as police chief. First of all, when were you actually appointed police chief?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: On the 28th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About a month before, had you been to any other meeting?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What meeting was that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This was the meeting where the Serb Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo was proclaimed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown P11?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: P what? MR. DI FAZIO: P11. May I see it before it's handed to the witness?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just -- I'd like you to have a read of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Of the whole document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just reacquaint yourself, just read through it quickly and just see what it's all about first of all.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have to read it in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, what is the title of P11 is that we know what it is too. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I understand Your Honour's concern. I think it should be called "Decision on the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac," dated 29th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that document referring to the meeting you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did that meeting take place? I'm talking about the meeting, this document refers to, the one on the 29th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This meeting took place in the large hall of the memorial centre in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Blagoje Simic attend?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the other defendants attend? I mean Mr. Tadic and Mr. Simo Zaric. If you don't know, say so, but if you do know that they attended, let us know.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I do not recollect. I know that Mr. Simic was there but I don't recall about the other two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Milan Simic? Can you tell us if he was there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Milan Simic was not there at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at Article 5, please. That says that this new assembly of Serbian people of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo will consist of members, board members, of the Serbian Democratic Party or SDS. And goes on to say that members of other boards of Serbian people may also become members by signing a statement announcing their membership in the assembly. Do you remember that decision being taken?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is signed by Ilija Ristic, president of the assembly. Who is he?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Ilija Ristic at the time was the president of that assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he -- where was he living?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the SDS, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I've done with that document, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, maybe approximately 100 people or more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it publicly -- withdraw that question. Was the fact of the meeting and its decision taking process and its decisions made publicly known? Was it open for people to know and understand what had been decided or was it a secret meeting?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it wasn't a secret meeting. It was generally known, and it wasn't at all a secret meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if it was commented upon in the media?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I do not recall, but as far as I remember, it was a generally known fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like you to turn to the meeting that took place a month later, that is on the 29th or -- late February. Where did that meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Up until now, we were speaking about the meeting on the 28th of February. Are you now considering the meeting in March?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise to you. I misled you. I realise we were talking about the meeting in February. I now want to direct your attention to the meeting in late March?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is 1992, I take it? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is first of all where did the meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That meeting was held in the village of Obudovac

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many people were there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: According to my assessment, 60, 70 people were present, maybe a bit more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there SDS members there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe members of the SDS and as far as I recall, maybe a few people from other parties, but of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if -- what proportion of attending people who attended were members of the SDS? Most of them? Just a few of them?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, the bigger part came from SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Blagoje Simic present?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Miroslav Tadic present?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall of seeing Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this meeting, did the issue of an appointment of a Serbian police chief arise?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber how it came about that the issue was first raised and how it developed?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: You are considering the raising the question of the appointment or does it apply to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you've told us the issue of the appointment of a police chief arose at the meeting. Tell the Chamber how it arose at the meeting, what was decided, how the matter was proceeded with, at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: First, at the meeting, were the municipal delegates of the four municipalities were present, Pero Stevic was proposed as a police chief, but later, some other assembly -- municipal assembly members refused that candidate, and proposed me, and with a majority vote of the municipal assembly members with a majority of their votes, I was appointed to the post of police chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who proposed you, can you recall?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember whether it was Ilija Ristic who proposed me or Lazar Stanisic. I can not recall precisely who of the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were delegates of the four municipalities. Who were these delegates and which municipalities are you talking about? Delegates from what? That's what I want to know. And from where.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They were legally elected municipal delegates, elected legally at the earlier multi-party elections, who worked in the assemblies of or Orasje, Gradacac, some Samac municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were already members of the municipal assemblies that are always existed in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were members of these legally formed assemblies, after the first, regular, multi-party elections, held in Bosnia, I believe held in the year 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And they were all of Serb ethnicity, I take it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And it was those people who voted eventually for your appointment as police chief?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently receive any instructions as to how you should go about organising yourself as police chief, what you should be doing, any moves or measures that you should be taking?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The -- during the first few days, no. A few days later, I received instructions to supply blue berets for the police, and with the presence of the president of the municipal council, I did talk in the village of Obudovac, to the reserve police force in that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all ethnic Serbs?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The majority were Serbs. Only the deputy chief police of the reserve police force in the village of Obudovac was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: His nickname was "Caba" but I do not recall his exact name and surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll come to the blue berets, later but first of all the talk that you gave, what was that about and what was your purpose in giving this talk?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, prior to that meeting, President Mirko Jovanovic told me that that police station, which I will be heading, will have its headquarters in Obudovac, as well as the new Serb municipality which would be set up there if things turned for the worse. And during that meeting with these members of the police, which was attended by Mirko Jovanovic also, he held a short speech and as far as I recall, he said that the republican deputies in Sarajevo proclaimed the Republic of -- Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. After that the autonomous region of Bosnia was proclaimed. And in Samac, on the 26th, 27th of February, the Serb Municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo, which was being founded, and Stevan Todorovic was appointed for this region, for the police, and he said, if people -- if the problem will not be resolved democratically, politically, then you will be under the command of Stevan Todorovic, who is the police chief in this area. That was approximately the content of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In effect, he was announcing you to the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you make -- sorry, I'll withdraw that. Did you make any practical arrangements for the possibility of you becoming the new police chief? For example, recruitment, anything like that? Apart from blue berets. I'll get to that later. But did you make any other sort of practical arrangements?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In addition to purchasing these blue berets, I didn't undertake any other practical measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about subordinates in the new Serb police force? Did you make arrangements to appoint anyone to be your subordinate, interview anyone, speak to anyone?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I didn't have any subordinates yet because up until the 17th of April, I was only a police chief on paper, without any aides and people working under me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I mean is prior to that, did you speak to anyone and say, "In case of this matter -- in case this Serb police force coming into existence and my actively becoming the chief of the Serb police, "I want to you be there working with me"? Did you make any such arrangements?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At that meeting, at Obudovac, which was attended by Mirko Jovanovic, I also spoke and I said, "If the situation will turn for the worse, if we don't find a democratic, political solution," I said, "Will you be accepting this command?" And then they said, "Well, no problem. We are here."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you said you wanted to -- rather you did purchase blue berets. Where did you go to buy those?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: These blue berets I bought in a shop in Belgrade. It's where they sold these berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from your appointment as police chief, or rather announcement of your appointment as police chief, were there any other announcements regarding administrative positions or appointments made at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In addition to my appointment as police chief, then the chief of the Department of Defence was appointed, and as I also mentioned, that I did not have any experience in police work, I would ask them to appoint somebody else with greater experience. They said, "You will be the police chief." And they appointed three assistants, Predic Stevic, Milan Stankovic, and Milan Petrovic. They were appointed as my assistants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said Blagoje Simic was present at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he appointed to any position?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At that meeting, they asked Blagoje Simic to form the Crisis Staff, and as he -- he stated, they stated they believed there won't be a need for that, but they agreed that if the need arises, that he be then the President of that Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he accept that? Agree to become president, if the need arose?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He didn't oppose it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he give any speeches at this meeting or say anything?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At this point in time, I do not recall concretely the speech. Probably he did make a statement, but at this point in time, I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. I'd like to turn now to another topic. It's generally accepted that in Bosanski Samac there was a military body called the 4th Detachment. Was there also in the area a 1st, 2nd and 3rd Detachment as well?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they based?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Detachment was based in -- with headquarters in the village of Batkusa. The second one in the village of Crkvina. And the 3rd Detachment in the village of Pelagicevo. And the 4th Detachment in the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you have any role in any of those detachments?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had a role in the 1st Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was the assistant of the commander of the 1st Detachment for intelligence and security matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the other detachments have a similar position? Namely a position dealing with intelligence and security matters?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was filling that position in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In the 4th Detachment, it was Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Detachments were they all part of a larger military unit, the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 17th Tactical Group as at April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel active officer Stevan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the 17th Tactical Group based at the time? In early 1992?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The command headquarters of the 17th Tactical Group was located in the village Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have a supply dump or an area where they kept all their weapons, ammunition, supplies and so on?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they had a small dump, smaller warehouse, in Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these various detachments, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th, ever deal with one another, that is share information, intelligence, have conferences, that sort of thing? Did they cooperate closely with one another?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do not recall that there was any official exchange of information but the information was submitted to the intelligence unit of the 17th Tactical Group, but maybe there was some oral exchange of a lesser volume. It could have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it your duty, as assistant to the commander for intelligence and security matters, to report to the 17th Tactical Group on such matters?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That was the duty, but I don't recall of submitting any written document. Maybe a few oral ones, because I wasn't a professional in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like now to turn to another topic, and that is the issue of paramilitaries. Do you know a place called Batkusa? I think you've already mentioned it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did paramilitaries ever arrive there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What date did they arrive there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I believe on the 11th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many paramilitaries arrived there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: If I recall, a total of 50 members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman nicknamed Crni?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I met him at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's his full name, can you recall?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I believe his full name is Dragan Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in the group of paramilitaries that arrived at Batkusa?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know another man, nicknamed "Lugar"?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I met him also on that 11th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, can you remember Lugar's full -- full name? If you can't, don't worry, but if you can remember, tell us.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I believe his name was Slobodan Miljkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were those two men from?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Crni was from Vranje, and Lugar and other 28 volunteers were from Kragujevac, also Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from your last answer both those places, Vranje and Kragujevac are both in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they arrive in Batkusa? How did they get there, in other words?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They arrived by helicopters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that JNA helicopter or air force helicopter? Part of the military service formations of the Yugoslavian army?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you actually there when they arrived? Were you there to greet them or not?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was there when they landed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the commander of the 1st detachment was there, Mico Ivanovic, nicknamed "Mijak". There were some other people there as well but I can't remember at this moment who else was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Ivanovic fellow, Mico, was he ever on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. He was not on the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Where did they set themselves up, the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The first night, they arrived in the afternoon, so the first night they set themselves up in the village of Batkusa, in the primary school there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did they have any sort of uniform or designation? Were they given a name?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They all had camouflage, NATO uniforms. They had Red Berets on their heads, and on the left or the right arm, they had a patch signifying a grey wolf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Di Fazio, I wonder we can clarify whether in that last answer, the witness actually said that they had camouflage NATO uniforms on. MR. DI FAZIO: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Is it correct? MR. DI FAZIO: I'll clarify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be absolutely clear, you said the way it came out in translation, Mr. Todorovic, it sounded like you said they had NATO uniforms on, which I doubt. Were you in fact saying they had NATO-like uniforms?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Their uniforms resembled NATO uniforms, and it was customary to say of those uniforms that they were NATO uniforms, although they had no NATO insignia on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the line of authority in this group of paramilitaries? Who was in charge and who was next in charge and so on? And also can you comment on tell us what position Lugar held in the group?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Crni had the highest position for those -- amongst those 30 men from Serbia. His assistant was Debeli. And then Lugar tried to be an assistant to Debeli.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Debeli is a nickname. I believe. Do you remember his full name?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. His nickname is Debeli and his name is Srecko Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The men who came, you said that there were about 50, but a number of them, I think you said 30 or so, came with Crni, what sort of differentiation are you making in the group?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: You mean in this group of 30 or the group of 50?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, in the group of 50, was it divided up in any particular way?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These 30 came exclusively from Serbia, and the other 20 were people from the municipality of Samac, who had been -- who had gone to training to Serbia and then they all came back together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll go into the 20 from Samac in due course but it's the 30 that came with Crni that I'm interested in. Do you know how they were selected, who assisted in their selection? How they were recruited?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: From what I heard from them, they registered for this kind of thing to wage war in Bosnia, in other words, through the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Crni have any connections, as far as you're aware, with the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about Crni. The others said that they did, and this Radovanovic man later was a republic delegate of the Serbian Radical Party in the Serbian parliament.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They arrived on the 11th of April. Did you see them again on the 12th of April?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Some of them, I did. I saw Crni again on the 12th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other military men or attend any meetings on the 12th of April?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic. I saw commander Mico Ivanovic. At this meeting at Agro Posavina [phoen] in Donji Zagon on the 12th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the defendants present?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was present of the defendants, and also Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, you're not a defendant in this case. So when I speak of the defendants, I'll just mention -- I'm referring to the other gentlemen what you identified earlier. Any way, you said that Blagoje Simic was present?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the meeting? What was discussed?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
