utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, from the very beginning, and I also received information that even before April 17th, there were people there and also that some weapons were placed on top -- up on top of the silos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your source of information regarding the snipers on top of the silos?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I had two kinds of information. The first piece I got from Mr. Dako Misic, who was responsible for technical security of this agricultural company that the silo is a part of, and he said that 4th Detachment members of Mr. Zaric changed locks a few days earlier on the silo and then later, about a month or two Mr. Simo Zaric told me this himself, that they had earlier brought weapons up to the top of the silo and that locks had been changed on certain doors in the silo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just in case it's not absolutely clear to the Chamber, what's the significance of the changing of locks at the silos?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, since at that time the manager of the silos was Marko Bozanovic, who was a Croat and a reserve captain, and he was also the commander of the Croatian and Muslim Territorial Defence, this changing was done without his knowledge. That is to say illegally. So that that night, people could enter the premises and go up to the top of the silo without asking for the real keys from the porter, and because -- and also the silo was the tallest building in the entire region, and from the top of the silo you had a very good view and a very good command of the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm interested in what Simo Zaric had to say to you about that. You said he discussed this matter with you about a month or two after. Was this at some point after the 16th and 17th of April, obviously?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, this was late May, early June. He said, "We have -- we put some weapons up there earlier, some members of the 4th Detachment did this. We put some weapons up on the top of the silos and we also changed the locks."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he come to say this to you? Was it in the course of some sort of report? Was it over drinks or was it a -- in passing? I just want to know in what context it was that he said this to you.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This was not an official report. At that time, people were talking about who had contributed the most to the liberation, and he was saying, "It's not these ones with colourful uniforms. It was us who did this. We changed the locks, we had the weapons, and we had brought the weapons up to the silo maybe about 20 or 30 days before." And this was just a private conversation that we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Todorovic, I just want to show you some documents. I want to produce to you this document. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, Defence counsel will know of it as C11 in the exhibit list. If Your Honours please, while we are waiting for the document to be presented, I don't know what your schedule is this afternoon. Do you want to keep going straight through to 5.30?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, we are sitting to 17 hours, it's one and a half hours. MR. DI FAZIO: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Todorovic, would you please have a look at that document?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's got a Crisis Staff stamp on it but no apparent signature. Was it nonetheless a Crisis Staff decision that was issued? Order, I should say.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was this order publicised or made known to those to whom it was directed?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I think it was broadcast on the local radio. I remember, however, that there was also a loud speaker used, not the entire order was read out but it was said through this loudspeaker that if -- whoever handed over their weapons in the next two hours, they would not have any problems. It was also said that the members of paramilitary Croatian and Muslim formations should hand over their weapons. And this was all said through the loudspeaker. It might also have been broadcast on the local radio but I'm not completely sure about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The document says that in paragraph -- just withdraw that question. Would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, the document says that the weapons and equipment have to be taken into the municipal crisis headquarters. That is the public security station. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: [no interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the reference there municipal crisis headquarters? Is that any particular body or is it the Crisis Staff? I just don't understand what the municipal crisis headquarters are.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Probably it refers to the premises of the Crisis Staff but as far as I know, all the weapons handed over were taken -- were taken and delivered by people to the public security station. I don't know that anybody took it to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is not my intention to interfere. Maybe just one suggestion. Maybe our learned friend can ask the witness just it read this paragraph 2 and then maybe it's a problem, I think it's a problem with translation. I guess. So maybe in order to clarify that issue maybe he can read paragraph 2 and then we'll see about what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Before you do that, Mr. Di Fazio, I think the witness has already assisted on this issue, because he said, as far as he knew, the weapons were taken to the public security station. And in fact that's what the paragraph says, as you can see. MR. DI FAZIO: That is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Municipal crisis headquarters, that is to the public security station. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful Your Honour it's a question of not being able to see the wood for the trees. I'm sorry I should have just read on. I don't think I need to clarify anything further. In fact I tender the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P77 ter for the B/C/S and P77 for the English version, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I have a no objection for the admissibility but to the authenticity, just for the record, because we don't know who is the author of this document and also of course, we shall have possibility in cross-examination to clarify this issue, also I have the objection to the translation of the English version of this document, which is absolutely contrary to what was said in B/C/S language, but my friend left that topic and it will be up to us to clarify that in cross-examination. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one matter, Mr. Todorovic, I'll show you the document again if you need to but there was a stamp on there. Did you recognise it? That is on P77. Did you recognise it as a Crisis Staff stamp? If you don't, can't remember, I'll show you the document again but do you remember the stamp?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: If you could show it to me once again, if it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. I'm sorry, I apologise for not directing your attention to it. MR. DI FAZIO: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P77?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the original, if you need to. You don't have to necessarily look at it on the television.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I will not be, I hope, repeating myself again. I'm not a handwriting specialist but it does look like the stamp of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask you now to look at this other document that I produce to you. And if Your Honours please, Defence counsel will know of this document as C52. Just acquaint yourself with the document, please. Okay. Have you had a chance to look at the document?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This one has a different stamp. Can you tell us what the stamp is?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It says the Serb Autonomous District of Semberija and Majevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thinking back to that time, is that what the -- let me rephrase my question. Were you familiar with that stamp, that is the stamp of the Serb or Serbian Autonomous District of Semberija and Majevica?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Let me say that I had few or none documents -- no document with such a stamp at the time. But I did know that -- of the existence of the Serb Autonomous District of Semberija and Majevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who the -- who this Stjepanovic mentioned at the bottom of the document is?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I heard that Mr. -- That person, Mr. Stjepanovic was the President of the Serbian Autonomous District of Semberija and Majevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what his first name was?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly but I do remember the surname, Stjepanovic. Maybe Milan, but I do know that it was -- that it's Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And were people required, as this document says, to hand over even legally owned weapons?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This is what is contained in this decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What I'm asking you is can you recall that people obeyed this decision, came in and started handing over their legally owned weapons?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do remember that people were handing over their legally owned weapons. That is pistols, for which they had a permit, as well as for hunting weapons, not all of them, but some did come in with these. MR. DI FAZIO: I produce the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the numbers, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P78 ter for the B/C/S version and P78 for the English version, Your Honours. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P36, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, can you identify the signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who gave you that document to sign? Did you create it or did someone give it to you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, this document was drafted by the legal expert, Mitar Mitrovic, but I signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean "legal expert, Mitar Mitrovic"? Was he a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He finished law school. He was a lawyer in the Crisis Staff, a member of the Crisis Staff, and he had a law degree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he charged with -- sorry, did he have the responsibility for dealing with legal matters that the Crisis Staff might be interested in? And also providing legal advice to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was a lawyer in the Crisis Staff. However, as the lady who was dealing with administrative affairs in the station, I believe it was he who drafted the document, typed it, and I signed it. So I stand behind the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Di Fazio, I'm afraid I don't have that particular exhibit P36 in front of me. Do you think you could have the -- we could have the English version just put on the ELMO for a moment just so that we know what the document is that the witness signed? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I'm sorry, I didn't realise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I don't have that particular one with me today. MR. DI FAZIO: I apologise for that. We will just attend to that now, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's already on the ELMO, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Oh, okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people come to you and get your written consent as it says they must in paragraph 1? If they wanted to get into and out of the town?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, they would be coming mainly Serbs who wished to go and visit their people in Serbia. They would come for this written consent, in order to be able to leave, go and visit, and then return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you attend to it each such application or did you sign numerous consents for them to leave the town?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't deal with each individual application, but if somebody had a wounded brother or son, they would receive such a written consent, and they could go for two or three days, to go and visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It refers to checkpoints being established. Were there checkpoints set up around the town soon after the 17th of April? Or indeed from the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mitar Mitrovic explain to you that -- or say to you who was the author of this document? I know that he said that he produced it, he gave it to you, but did he say whose idea it was? Was this it a Crisis Staff decision or was it his own idea? Have you got any idea -- do you have any knowledge as to that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know in concrete terms what exactly happened. I know I signed this. I know that the checkpoints were set up. And that the police station, which I was heading, we issued these written permits. But how the document was drafted, I couldn't tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Serbs, people of Serbian ethnic origin, might want to leave town, go and visit relatives, possibly relatives who had been wounded. Were Muslims and Croats permitted in the same way to leave the town?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, some Muslims or Croats who had also members in the 4th Detachment, they -- if they requested, they could get such consent, but as far as I know, Muslims, primarily, or it particularly Croats, couldn't enter Serbia because the Serbian authorities didn't allow them to enter Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that effectively mean that they were imprisoned in the town?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must object. I must object. This is absolutely leading question calling for conclusions which are absolutely beyond the standards of the examination-in-chief. Many, many ways how this question can be posed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's a leading question, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the effect of this order on Muslims and Croats who weren't in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me say that those who were not -- I remember a lady, a Muslim lady, who wanted to see her children and they were not in the 4th Detachment and she received the certificate and she went to Serbia to see her children. But the reason for drafting such an order was to prevent the soldiers, Serb soldiers, from deserting this territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you another document now. MR. DI FAZIO: Defence council will know of it as C13. Do Your Honours have copies of that document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, I'll quickly take you through this document. It's an announcement, and it refers to the Territorial Defence of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac preventing green berets and paramilitary units coming in from Croatia. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the reference to the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac? So far in your evidence you've described the activities of your police, the 4th Detachment, and the paramilitaries. But I haven't heard you refer to a Territorial Defence of the Serbian Municipality. What therefore is the document talking about when it uses that expression, Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: During the course of the first or the second month, more than one term was used for one formation, and in this part here, Territorial Defence of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac, it refers to the 4th, 3rd, 2nd and 1st detachments. I think it refers to that formation, but here in the document, it's described as Territorial Defence of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The document is presumably directed to the citizens of Bosanski Samac. That's what it says in fact in the first line. The -- other than the 4th Detachment, those other detachments, the 3rd, 2nd and 1st, they didn't participate in the takeover of the town, did they?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the 4th Detachment, as far as I know, also the 2nd Detachment participated, because it was located close by but the 1st and the 3rd did not but I do know that the 4th and the 2nd participated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the 2nd Detachment based in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that in fact is where you held the meeting on the night of the 16th, right?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was this document that I have just shown you made known to the people?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, this document was read out via the local radio station, Radio Samac. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I produce the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- A number of times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours it will be P79 ter for the B/C/S and P79 for the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, according to the position of the Defence, in the Pre-Trial face of course and now we have objection to the authenticity of this document, in details that the heading of this particular document was not typed, it was written by person, we don't know who and when, and the other objections with regard to the -- this particular issue are still in force so that the Prosecution can explain us in further proceedings chain of custody, et cetera. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: May I just have a moment to confer with my colleague about this matter if Your Honours please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you. If Your Honours please, as far as this particular document is concerned, I think Ms. Reidy will be able to -- I hope Ms. Reidy will be able to produce some documentation relating to Defence acceptance of this document in the past. Be that as it may, however, it's unnecessary, I submit, for Mr. Pantelic to announce each time a document goes in that he has doubts about its authenticity. He can attack it through the witness when his -- the time comes for his cross-examination. But as I said, Ms. Reidy will look into the matter and be able to inform the Chamber if there has been an acceptance of its authenticity in the past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we wait until that is done? MR. DI FAZIO: No, no. I seek its full admission now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes, I think the matters raised can be dealt with in the later proceedings and we will certainly go to the weight to it be attached to the document. Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm just referring to the letter that we sent to the Prosecution, and I'm going through that list, that's only for the record. I'm absolutely agree with the position of Trial Chamber. We know we are well aware that we shall discuss that in our case, it's just for the record. It's a matter of record, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I didn't have any other intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. All right. We will adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
